# gh-1555: [GOAL] Session JSONL grows unboundedly past the 2 GiB full-open backstop; legacy full-open call sites (picker, resume fallback, trajectory, subagent preview) make the session unopenable

## Description

## Goal — unbounded session JSONL growth defeats the 2 GiB full-open backstop (v1, initial draft)

One sentence: **every session remains openable forever at ANY size — 100 GB included — through lazy, tail-first, bounded-memory reads, and no ledger record is ever lost**: size is a read-pattern problem, never a deletion problem.

Today a session JSONL is append-only forever: compaction appends a summary record and never shrinks the file, and nothing rotates or trims by size. The gh-1073 backstop (`defaultMaxFullOpenBytes = 2 << 30`, lib/src/session/session_storage.dart:30) converted the old silent heap explosion into a loud `SessionException` refusal — but nothing on the write side slows growth and nothing on the read side migrates the legacy full-open call sites to the existing windowed reader. So every active named session is a ticking bomb: it works for weeks, then permanently falls off the picker/trajectory/resume-fallback paths. This happened in production on 2026-10-11 (incident below). This card changes both sides: all tail/preview/trajectory read paths migrate to windowed/token-budgeted opens, and the ledger gains a size-based rotation/trim plus write-side caps on the dominant growth drivers.

## Owner directive (2026-10-11, supersedes any size-budget thinking below)

- **Sessions are never lost.** Not by trim, not by rotation, not by repair, not by write-side cap applied retroactively. A 100 GB ledger is a valid ledger. Any solution whose size story involves deleting or truncating EXISTING records is rejected by definition.
- **Openability is unconditional.** Picker, resume, trajectory view, trajectory export, subagent preview — all must work on a 100 GB session with bounded memory. If a path cannot be made lazy, the path is buggy, not the session "too big".
- **Context-meter continuity across close/reopen.** A session closed showing 59% context usage reopens showing the same 59% — the resume boundary (newest compaction boundary, or the token-budget tail for a boundary-less marathon) must reconstruct EXACTLY the context the live loop carried at exit, not an approximation. Wrong boundary = wrong meter = a regression the owner can see.
- **Lazy loading everywhere, export included.** Today `exportTrajectoryJson`/`exportTrajectoryMarkdown` (lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_export.dart:16,33) take a fully materialized `TrajectorySnapshot` — pure functions over `snapshot.records`, no IO. That means export transitively requires the full open it should avoid. Export must become scan-and-emit streaming: read records in bounded chunks, serialize incrementally to the sink, never materialize the snapshot.
- **Forward-looking write-side reduction** (W3) is permitted ONLY as opt-in and only for FUTURE records, and even then is an owner-call open question — never the mechanism that makes old sessions openable.

## Why this framing

- **Retracted framing 1:** "just raise/disable the 2 GiB bound" — the bound exists because a 12 GiB session used to die with `Exhausted heap space` inside readTextFile (gh-1073); raising it re-opens the OOM. Retracted.
- **Retracted framing 2:** "compaction alone fixes size" — compaction APPENDS a summary record; it never shrinks the file. The "network" incident session reached 2.54 GiB with **zero** compaction records; the ssh/followup session reached 2.91 GB **with** 51 compaction records. Compaction reduces model context, not bytes on disk. Retracted.
- **Retracted framing 3:** "this is a read-side-only fix" — migrating call sites keeps the bomb ticking at 0.4–0.6 GB/week; the write side needs caps and a trim story. Retracted as insufficient (kept as the core tier, not the whole card).
- **Retracted framing 4:** "trim/rotate/delete old records to stay under a size budget" — owner directive 2026-10-11: the ledger is sacred, a 100 GB session must open, and no existing record may be lost. Rotation is allowed ONLY as split-and-retain (all `.part-NN` siblings kept and reassembled by the reader); repair keeps its `.bak` until the user explicitly removes it. Retracted.

## Incident (2026-10-11, all numbers measured with `stat -f %z` and `LC_ALL=C grep -c '"type":"compaction"'`)

The owner tried to open two sessions from the fa TUI session picker; both failed with `failed to open session <id>: SessionException: Refusing to open session <path>: … exceeds the 2.0 GiB full-open bound`:

| Session | Created | Bytes | Size | Compaction records |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `01a0d73f` ("network") | 2026-09-25 | 2,737,991,964 | 2.54 GiB | **0** in 2.7 GB of JSONL |
| `e7a689` (.worktrees/issue/355/ssh/followup) | 2026-09-14 | 2,912,096,469 | 2.91 GB | 51 |
| `01a06644` ("goal_builder") | 2026-09-03 | 2,236,083,302 | 2.08 GiB | 6 |

Sessions live under `~/Library/Group Containers/group.dev.fa1.shared/fa/sessions/<slug>/`. Measured growth: ~0.4–0.6 GB/week on active named sessions.

## Mechanism chain (pinned facts — each verified against the working tree 2026-10-11)

- **(a) Append-only forever.** Session JSONL grows monotonically; compaction appends a summary record and never shrinks the file; nothing rotates or trims by size.
- **(b) Growth drivers.** Measured on goal_builder's last 500 MB (10,196 records): hidden `model_request_summary` custom records ≈ **0.7 MB EACH** (one per outbound LLM request — they persist a request-detail snapshot for the trajectory Request tab), plus multi-MB toolResult records (full test-run logs). Top records in the chunk: one 1.5 MB toolResult, then an unbroken run of 0.7 MB model_request_summary records.
- **(c) The windowed tail-reader EXISTS and is the intended design.** `WindowedSessionStorage.open` via `SessionRepo.open(metadata, windowed: true)` at lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:343 (doc comment: "the app's chat path, issue #135 … only the header plus the newest chunk are materialized"). The CLI resume `_loadSession` opens windowed (lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart:582) and pages back only to the newest compaction boundary under a token budget (`ensureCompactionBoundaryResident`, gh-968 parity budget).
- **(d) BUT seven legacy call sites still take the DEFAULT full open (windowed:false):**
  1. lib/src/cli/agent_cli_pickers.dart:74 — TUI session picker `_tuiPickSession` does `_repo.open(metadata)`; the catch at :82 prints exactly the observed `failed to open session <id>: SessionException: Refusing to open session …`. **← the user's exact failure path.**
  2. lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart:611 — `_loadSession` full-open FALLBACK when `ensureCompactionBoundaryResident` returns false (a marathon with NO compaction boundary). The "network" session has 0 compaction records → even the main resume path degenerates to full open → guaranteed refusal past 2 GiB.
  3. lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart:196 — `_resumeLastSession` full open.
  4. lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart:492 — name-resolution fallback loop, full-open PER SESSION until name match.
  5. lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart:64,67,71 — `fa trajectory view/tail/cost/inspect` resolve via `repo.open(metadata)` full.
  6. bin/fah_trajectory.dart:94 — headless trajectory full open.
  7. lib/src/cli/agent_commands.dart:314 — `_openChildSession` (subagent transcript preview) full open.
- **(e) The backstop itself.** `defaultMaxFullOpenBytes = 2 << 30` (lib/src/session/session_storage.dart:30); refusal thrown at :641 and :752 with `SessionErrorCode.tooLarge` (gh-1073 — added because a 12 GiB session used to die with `Exhausted heap space` inside readTextFile).

### Amplification

The backstop converted a silent heap explosion into a loud refusal — but nothing on the WRITE side slows growth, and nothing on the READ side migrates the legacy call sites to windowed. So every long-lived named session is a ticking bomb: it works for weeks, then permanently falls off the picker/trajectory/resume-fallback paths. The gh-1073 refusal message even prescribes `fa --session …` and `fa session repair` — both of which themselves degenerate to a refused full open when the session has no compaction boundary (mechanism d2), so the documented rescue is broken for exactly the worst cases.

## Architecture

Three named workstreams, each independently shippable, in priority order:

- **W1 — Lazy/windowed-everywhere reads (the spine).** Every read path that needs only tail/preview/metadata opens windowed. The picker needs only name+metadata (never transcript). Trajectory view pages through the ledger instead of materializing a whole-snapshot. The `_loadSession` fallback (d2) pages by **token budget** — `resumeParityBudget` — instead of requiring a compaction boundary: a marathon without compaction must tail-read the last N tokens, not full-open. **Trajectory export joins this tier as scan-and-emit streaming** (owner directive): the exporters stop taking a materialized `TrajectorySnapshot` and instead serialize from a bounded record stream straight to the sink. **Invariant:** every user-facing read path — picker, resume, trajectory view, trajectory export, subagent preview — runs in memory bounded by the window/chunk, independent of ledger size; a 100 GB session opens and exports. `defaultMaxFullOpenBytes` becomes reachable only by explicit repair tooling, never by a user-facing path.
- **W2 — Split-and-retain rotation (never discard).** Size-based rotation per gh-1077 (`.part-NN` siblings) where EVERY segment is retained on disk and the reader reassembles the full logical ledger across segments — rotation changes file layout, never content. `fa session repair` may compact-in-place ONLY with the pre-rewrite ledger preserved as a sibling archive kept until the user explicitly deletes it (no TTL auto-delete). **Invariant:** after rotation or repair, `cat` of all segments/archives in order reproduces a superset of the pre-operation records — total record loss is provably zero.
- **W3 — Forward-only write-side reduction (opt-in, owner-call).** IF the owner enables it: spill oversized NEW `model_request_summary`/toolResult payloads to sibling blob files referenced by path (content stays, only its location moves — no truncation, no summary in place of data). This slows growth; it is never required for openability (W1 guarantees that at any size) and never touches existing records. **Invariant:** with W3 on, steady-state growth drops materially below the 0.4–0.6 GB/week baseline; with W3 off, everything still works at 100 GB.

Fallback paths: windowed open failure degrades to the picker listing the session with a "too large to preview" badge rather than a hard error; repair remains available for W2 recovery.

## Capability surface (everything a session-ledger lifecycle allows → our shape)

| Surface | Core (this card) | Second tier | Excluded (rationale) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Read: picker metadata/name | windowed (d1) | — | — |
| Read: resume | windowed + token-budget paging (d2, d3) | — | — |
| Read: name-resolution scan | windowed/batch (d4) | repo batch name API | — |
| Read: trajectory view/tail/cost/inspect (TUI + headless) | windowed/paged (d5, d6) | — | — |
| Read: subagent preview | windowed tail (d7) | — | — |
| Write: model_request_summary | cap/summarize payload | offload request detail to blob store | dropping the records entirely (breaks trajectory Request tab) |
| Write: toolResult persistence | size cap + spill/truncate marker | full blob CAS for large payloads | — |
| Ledger: rotation | activate/extend gh-1077 `.part-NN` by size | — | — |
| Ledger: repair | `fa session repair` compaction-in-place rewrite | online background trim | auto-trim without user opt-in (data-loss risk without a trash/backup step) |
| Backstop | unchanged (2 GiB, gh-1073) | — | raising/removing the bound (re-opens the 12 GiB OOM) |

## Pinned facts with positive AND negative tests

- **F1** — `defaultMaxFullOpenBytes == 2 << 30` (lib/src/session/session_storage.dart:30). POS: unit test asserts the constant and that a 2 GiB+1 byte synthetic ledger refuses with `SessionErrorCode.tooLarge`. NEG: a ledger below the bound still full-opens byte-identically (no behavior change for small sessions).
- **F2** — Windowed open materializes only header + newest chunk (lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:343). POS: open a synthetic 10 MB ledger windowed, assert resident record count < total and newest records present. NEG: assert the windowed session's parsed tail is byte-identical to the full open's tail on the same fixture (semantic-drift property test).
- **F3** — Picker path (lib/src/cli/agent_cli_pickers.dart:74) is the observed failure site. POS: fixture session > 2 GiB → picker lists it, opens windowed, shows name, no `SessionException`. NEG: a genuinely CORRUPT (not merely large) session still reports inline via the :82 catch — the error UX is preserved, not swallowed.
- **F4** — `_loadSession` fallback (lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart:611) must page by token budget, not require compaction. POS: marathon fixture with 0 compaction records and size > window → resume succeeds, resident context ≤ `resumeParityBudget`, and the resumed meter sits at/below window − reserve (gh-968 parity preserved). NEG: with a compaction boundary present, behavior is byte-identical to today (paging stops at the boundary).
- **F5** — `model_request_summary` ≈ 0.7 MB each is the dominant growth driver (measured: unbroken run of 0.7 MB records in goal_builder's last 500 MB). POS: after W3 caps, a recorded N-request workload produces ledger bytes strictly below a pinned threshold and every persisted summary ≤ cap. NEG: the trajectory Request tab still renders request detail for capped records (degraded-but-present, never empty).
- **F6** — Compaction never shrinks the file (incident: 51 compactions, 2.91 GB). POS: compaction-in-place repair REWRITES the ledger and `stat` size strictly decreases. NEG: post-repair replay (buildContext from the newest boundary) is record-identical to pre-repair replay of the same branch.
- **Degradation paths:** windowed open of a truncated/corrupt tail → inline error + repair hint (never a crash); repair on a session with 0 compaction records → falls back to token-budget tail rewrite with an explicit backup copy first; cap spill blob missing → trajectory renders the size marker instead of the payload.

## Security threat model

Attacker-controlled inputs here are limited but real: session JSONL content can contain untrusted page text, tool output, and file names harvested during agent runs. Threats specific to this card:

- **Exhaustion/OOM:** an oversized or adversarially-grown ledger must never again be fully materialized. Impossible-by-construction: after W1, no user-facing API exposes an unbounded full-open; the bound stays enforced inside the storage layer.
- **Data loss (the owner's #1 stated concern):** no path in this card may delete an existing ledger record. Rotation is split-and-retain: all `.part-NN` siblings persist and the reader reassembles them (a missing segment fails LOUD, never silently truncates the logical ledger). Repair writes the replacement to a NEW file, fsyncs, atomically renames, and keeps the pre-rewrite archive until the user explicitly deletes it — no TTL auto-delete, and repair never runs implicitly on open. A crash mid-repair leaves the original byte-identical.
- **Spill-blob smuggling (W3):** capped payloads spilled to sibling files are DATA: they are never interpreted as instructions, never executed, and are byte-scanned in tests to assert no secret-bearing record is written to a spill path without the ledger's provenance marker.
- **Instruction hierarchy:** nothing in this card lets ledger content authorize an action; ledger text can request, never grant. Model obedience is hygiene; the 2 GiB bound, atomic-rename repair, and provenance markers are the boundary.
- **Fixtures:** real incident payloads (the three sessions' record samples) become corpus fixtures, treated as DATA, never instructions.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — Picker opens a > 2 GiB session (windowed) and shows its name/metadata without a SessionException. (IT-1, E2E-1)
- **AC2** — Resume of a marathon session with 0 compaction records and > 2 GiB succeeds via token-budget tail paging; resumed context meter ≤ window − reserve (gh-968 parity). (IT-2, E2E-2)
- **AC3** — `fa trajectory view/tail/cost/inspect` (TUI and `bin/fah_trajectory.dart`) operate on a > 2 GiB session. (IT-3, E2E-3)
- **AC3a** — Trajectory export (JSON and Markdown) streams: on the oversize fixture, export completes with peak RSS bounded by a pinned multiple of the window size (not of the ledger size), and the emitted document round-trips every ledger record losslessly. (IT-3a, E2E-3a)
- **AC4** — Subagent transcript preview (`_openChildSession`) renders the tail of a > 2 GiB child session. (IT-4)
- **AC5** — `fa session repair` never loses a record: the pre-rewrite ledger survives as a sibling archive until the user explicitly deletes it, replay of the post-boundary branch is byte-identical, and `cat` of archive + new ledger reproduces the full pre-repair record set. (IT-5, E2E-4)
- **AC8** — The big-ledger invariant: openability and bounded memory must be PROVEN on real big sessions, not asserted from small fixtures. Unit/integration tests use small/medium sparse fixtures (just-over-2 GiB class — sparse files are disk-cheap and tail-reads stay fast); the extreme scale (100 GB-class sparse ledger, generated at test time, never committed) runs ONLY in E2E/nightly on a real host, plus validation against the three real incident sessions (2.08–2.91 GB) as the corpus. No unit test may allocate or materialize a giant fixture. (IT-7, E2E-6)
- **AC6** — After write-side caps, a recorded N-request workload grows the ledger below a pinned bytes/week threshold vs. the 0.4–0.6 GB/week baseline, and every `model_request_summary`/toolResult record respects its cap. (IT-6, E2E-5)
- **AC7** — Sessions below 2 GiB behave byte-identically to today on every touched path (no regressions for the common case). (REG-1..REG-4)
- **AC9** — Meter continuity (owner directive): closing a session at N% context usage and reopening it shows the SAME N% (±0): the resumed context equals what the live loop carried at exit. Boundary selection is deterministic — newest compaction boundary when present, token-budget tail otherwise — and the resumed footer/meter matches the pre-close reading on every fixture. (IT-8, E2E-7)

## Test plan

### Test matrix — maximal coverage, zero cross-platform breakage

- `UT-1` (AC-, F1): pure test of `defaultMaxFullOpenBytes` constant + refusal `SessionErrorCode.tooLarge` on synthetic oversize metadata (no IO).
- `UT-2` (W3): cap/summarize logic for `model_request_summary` and toolResult payloads — pure functions on record fixtures, incl. a payload exactly at cap and cap+1 byte.
- `UT-3` (W2): repair rewrite planner — given a record stream + boundary, the emitted stream equals the post-boundary prefix; property-tested on randomized synthetic ledgers.
- `IT-1` (AC1): fake repo + > 2 GiB sparse fixture file; picker opens windowed, name resolves, no exception; corrupt-file variant still hits the inline error line.
- `IT-2` (AC2, F4): fake windowed storage + marathon fixture (0 compactions) with deterministic clock; assert token-budget paging and parity-budget residency; variant WITH a boundary asserts unchanged behavior.
- `IT-3` (AC3): trajectory commands against the sparse oversize fixture, TUI resolver and headless `bin/fah_trajectory.dart` path both.
- `IT-3a` (AC3a): streaming export over the oversize fixture — peak RSS sampled during export stays under the pinned bound; the JSON export re-parses to the identical record sequence (losslessness property).
- `IT-7` (AC8): just-over-2 GiB sparse fixture (disk-cheap: holes + a real tail of records) — picker/resume/trajectory/export each complete under pinned RSS+wall-clock budgets. Small by construction; the point is crossing the backstop, not stressing CI.
- `IT-8` (AC9): record the live context meter before exit on deterministic fixtures (with and without a compaction boundary), resume, assert the reopened meter equals the recorded value exactly; a seeded wrong-boundary variant (off-by-one-boundary fixture) MUST fail this test.
- `IT-4` (AC4): `_openChildSession` tail preview on oversize child fixture.
- `IT-5` (AC5, F6): repair on a fixture with compactions strictly shrinks bytes; replay-equivalence assertion; `.bak` lifecycle; abort-midway (simulated crash between write and rename) leaves the original intact.
- `IT-6` (AC6, F5): recorded N-request workload through the real write path with caps on; assert per-record caps and total-byte threshold; byte-scan serialized payloads asserting no unmarked spill blobs.
- `E2E-1` (AC1): real host, real 2.54 GiB-class fixture (generated, not committed) — open via the TUI picker.
- `E2E-2` (AC2): resume the generated marathon fixture via `fa --session`.
- `E2E-3` (AC3): `fa trajectory tail` on the oversize fixture.
- `E2E-3a` (AC3a): real-host streaming export of the oversize fixture to disk; verify output size ≈ logical ledger size and zero snapshot materialization (RSS profile).
- `E2E-6` (AC8): nightly/real-host only — the 100 GB-class sparse fixture generated at test time (never committed) — full open-surface walk; PLUS the three real incident sessions (2.08–2.91 GB, copied aside before any repair) as the standing validation corpus.
- `E2E-7` (AC9): real host — run a session to a known context percentage, exit, reopen, screenshot/assert the meter reads the same percentage.
- `E2E-4` (AC5): `fa session repair` on a copy of the fixture; size drops; session opens afterwards.
- `E2E-5` (AC6): 24h-style simulated workload (compressed time) measures growth rate vs. baseline.
- `REG-1` (AC7): shared session-lifecycle suite runs through BOTH old (small session, full open) and new (windowed) paths with a semantic-drift property test asserting identical parsed context.
- `REG-2` (AC7, AC9): gh-968 resume parity suite — resumed meter ≤ window − reserve on every fixture, old and new, AND equals the pre-close meter exactly (AC9) on fixtures recorded with their live reading.
- `REG-3` (AC7): gh-1073 backstop suite — refusal behavior unchanged for repair tooling paths.
- `REG-4`: CLI/app/headless sibling surfaces (picker, `fa trajectory`, `bin/fah_trajectory`, subagent preview) all run the oversize fixture.

**CI wiring / merge rule:** UT+IT run on every PR; E2E oversize fixtures run nightly and on demand via a tag; REG jobs run on every PR touching `lib/src/session/**` or `lib/src/cli/**`. **A red REG job blocks merge even when all IT/E2E are green.**

### Edge / border cases

- **E1** — Session exactly at 2 GiB (boundary): opens full today; must still open after W1 with identical content.
- **E2** — Marathon with 0 compaction records > 2 GiB (the "network" shape): resume tails by token budget; picker/trajectory work; repair offers tail-rewrite with backup.
- **E3** — Kill/crash mid-repair: original ledger intact, partial replacement file cleaned on next open; never a half-renamed state.
- **E4** — Rotation boundary mid-record: a record is never split across `.part-NN` siblings; reader reassembles or refuses loudly.
- **E5** — False-positive "too large" on a sparse/compressed file: the bound measures logical size; picker degradation badge appears instead of a hard failure.
- **E6** — Capped `model_request_summary` requested by trajectory Request tab: renders the capped/summarized detail with a visible truncation marker, never an empty pane.
- **E7** — Name-resolution scan (d4) over MANY oversize sessions: bounded total time/memory (windowed per session), no O(N × full-open).
- **E8** — Repair on a session currently open by a live agent: refused with a clear message (no concurrent rewrite).

## Non-goals

- The freeze incident itself (crap4dart mutation runs) is **not** this card's scope.
- No change to the 2 GiB bound value or its refusal semantics (gh-1073 stays; retracted framing 1).
- No new chat/picker UI — the app IS the UI; this card changes open semantics, not presentation, beyond the degradation badge.
- No deletion of `model_request_summary` records outright (retracted — the trajectory Request tab depends on them); only caps/summarization/spill.
- **No size fix that loses existing ledger records** — no trim-to-budget, no auto-trim, no retroactive truncation or summarization of persisted records (owner directive 2026-10-11). W3, if adopted, is forward-only and opt-in.
- No automatic/implicit trimming on open; rewrites require explicit `fa session repair` and preserve the original as an archive.
- gh-1077 `.part-NN` rotation and gh-1073 backstop are **related work to reference/extend**, not re-implemented from scratch.

## Open questions

- W2 rotation trigger: size threshold per segment vs. per-session record count — owner call (both are split-and-retain; nothing is discarded either way).
- Streaming export sink API: exporters take a `Sink`/`StreamConsumer` and a record `Stream` — does the snapshot-based API stay for small sessions (dual API) or is everything unified on streaming?
- W3 adoption at all (opt-in blob spill for future records) — owner call; openability never depends on it.

## References

- gh-1073 (full-open backstop + `SessionErrorCode.tooLarge`), gh-1077 (`.part-NN` segment rotation), gh-968 (resume parity budget), gh-135 (windowed chat path), #503 (resume token-budget directive).

# gh-1555: [GOAL] Session JSONL grows unboundedly past the 2 GiB full-open backstop; legacy full-open call sites (picker, resume fallback, trajectory, subagent preview) make the session unopenable

## Description

## Goal — unbounded session JSONL growth defeats the 2 GiB full-open backstop (v1, initial draft)

One sentence: **every session remains openable forever at ANY size — 100 GB included — through lazy, tail-first, bounded-memory reads, and no ledger record is ever lost**: size is a read-pattern problem, never a deletion problem.

Today a session JSONL is append-only forever: compaction appends a summary record and never shrinks the file, and nothing rotates or trims by size. The gh-1073 backstop (`defaultMaxFullOpenBytes = 2 << 30`, lib/src/session/session_storage.dart:30) converted the old silent heap explosion into a loud `SessionException` refusal — but nothing on the write side slows growth and nothing on the read side migrates the legacy full-open call sites to the existing windowed reader. So every active named session is a ticking bomb: it works for weeks, then permanently falls off the picker/trajectory/resume-fallback paths. This happened in production on 2026-10-11 (incident below). This card changes both sides: all tail/preview/trajectory read paths migrate to windowed/token-budgeted opens, and the ledger gains a size-based rotation/trim plus write-side caps on the dominant growth drivers.

## Owner directive (2026-10-11, supersedes any size-budget thinking below)

- **Sessions are never lost.** Not by trim, not by rotation, not by repair, not by write-side cap applied retroactively. A 100 GB ledger is a valid ledger. Any solution whose size story involves deleting or truncating EXISTING records is rejected by definition.
- **Openability is unconditional.** Picker, resume, trajectory view, trajectory export, subagent preview — all must work on a 100 GB session with bounded memory. If a path cannot be made lazy, the path is buggy, not the session "too big".
- **Context-meter continuity across close/reopen.** A session closed showing 59% context usage reopens showing the same 59% — the resume boundary (newest compaction boundary, or the token-budget tail for a boundary-less marathon) must reconstruct EXACTLY the context the live loop carried at exit, not an approximation. Wrong boundary = wrong meter = a regression the owner can see.
- **Lazy loading everywhere, export included.** Today `exportTrajectoryJson`/`exportTrajectoryMarkdown` (lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_export.dart:16,33) take a fully materialized `TrajectorySnapshot` — pure functions over `snapshot.records`, no IO. That means export transitively requires the full open it should avoid. Export must become scan-and-emit streaming: read records in bounded chunks, serialize incrementally to the sink, never materialize the snapshot.
- **Forward-looking write-side reduction** (W3) is permitted ONLY as opt-in and only for FUTURE records, and even then is an owner-call open question — never the mechanism that makes old sessions openable.

## Why this framing

- **Retracted framing 1:** "just raise/disable the 2 GiB bound" — the bound exists because a 12 GiB session used to die with `Exhausted heap space` inside readTextFile (gh-1073); raising it re-opens the OOM. Retracted.
- **Retracted framing 2:** "compaction alone fixes size" — compaction APPENDS a summary record; it never shrinks the file. The "network" incident session reached 2.54 GiB with **zero** compaction records; the ssh/followup session reached 2.91 GB **with** 51 compaction records. Compaction reduces model context, not bytes on disk. Retracted.
- **Retracted framing 3:** "this is a read-side-only fix" — migrating call sites keeps the bomb ticking at 0.4–0.6 GB/week; the write side needs caps and a trim story. Retracted as insufficient (kept as the core tier, not the whole card).
- **Retracted framing 4:** "trim/rotate/delete old records to stay under a size budget" — owner directive 2026-10-11: the ledger is sacred, a 100 GB session must open, and no existing record may be lost. Rotation is allowed ONLY as split-and-retain (all `.part-NN` siblings kept and reassembled by the reader); repair keeps its `.bak` until the user explicitly removes it. Retracted.

## Incident (2026-10-11, all numbers measured with `stat -f %z` and `LC_ALL=C grep -c '"type":"compaction"'`)

The owner tried to open two sessions from the fa TUI session picker; both failed with `failed to open session <id>: SessionException: Refusing to open session <path>: … exceeds the 2.0 GiB full-open bound`:

| Session | Created | Bytes | Size | Compaction records |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `01a0d73f` ("network") | 2026-09-25 | 2,737,991,964 | 2.54 GiB | **0** in 2.7 GB of JSONL |
| `e7a689` (.worktrees/issue/355/ssh/followup) | 2026-09-14 | 2,912,096,469 | 2.91 GB | 51 |
| `01a06644` ("goal_builder") | 2026-09-03 | 2,236,083,302 | 2.08 GiB | 6 |

Sessions live under `~/Library/Group Containers/group.dev.fa1.shared/fa/sessions/<slug>/`. Measured growth: ~0.4–0.6 GB/week on active named sessions.

## Mechanism chain (pinned facts — each verified against the working tree 2026-10-11)

- **(a) Append-only forever.** Session JSONL grows monotonically; compaction appends a summary record and never shrinks the file; nothing rotates or trims by size.
- **(b) Growth drivers.** Measured on goal_builder's last 500 MB (10,196 records): hidden `model_request_summary` custom records ≈ **0.7 MB EACH** (one per outbound LLM request — they persist a request-detail snapshot for the trajectory Request tab), plus multi-MB toolResult records (full test-run logs). Top records in the chunk: one 1.5 MB toolResult, then an unbroken run of 0.7 MB model_request_summary records.
- **(c) The windowed tail-reader EXISTS and is the intended design.** `WindowedSessionStorage.open` via `SessionRepo.open(metadata, windowed: true)` at lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:343 (doc comment: "the app's chat path, issue #135 … only the header plus the newest chunk are materialized"). The CLI resume `_loadSession` opens windowed (lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart:582) and pages back only to the newest compaction boundary under a token budget (`ensureCompactionBoundaryResident`, gh-968 parity budget).
- **(d) BUT seven legacy call sites still take the DEFAULT full open (windowed:false):**
  1. lib/src/cli/agent_cli_pickers.dart:74 — TUI session picker `_tuiPickSession` does `_repo.open(metadata)`; the catch at :82 prints exactly the observed `failed to open session <id>: SessionException: Refusing to open session …`. **← the user's exact failure path.**
  2. lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart:611 — `_loadSession` full-open FALLBACK when `ensureCompactionBoundaryResident` returns false (a marathon with NO compaction boundary). The "network" session has 0 compaction records → even the main resume path degenerates to full open → guaranteed refusal past 2 GiB.
  3. lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart:196 — `_resumeLastSession` full open.
  4. lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart:492 — name-resolution fallback loop, full-open PER SESSION until name match.
  5. lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart:64,67,71 — `fa trajectory view/tail/cost/inspect` resolve via `repo.open(metadata)` full.
  6. bin/fah_trajectory.dart:94 — headless trajectory full open.
  7. lib/src/cli/agent_commands.dart:314 — `_openChildSession` (subagent transcript preview) full open.
- **(e) The backstop itself.** `defaultMaxFullOpenBytes = 2 << 30` (lib/src/session/session_storage.dart:30); refusal thrown at :641 and :752 with `SessionErrorCode.tooLarge` (gh-1073 — added because a 12 GiB session used to die with `Exhausted heap space` inside readTextFile).

### Amplification

The backstop converted a silent heap explosion into a loud refusal — but nothing on the WRITE side slows growth, and nothing on the READ side migrates the legacy call sites to windowed. So every long-lived named session is a ticking bomb: it works for weeks, then permanently falls off the picker/trajectory/resume-fallback paths. The gh-1073 refusal message even prescribes `fa --session …` and `fa session repair` — both of which themselves degenerate to a refuse…

## General PR Comments

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):

🚨 **BLOCKING: `fa trajectory tail` goes permanently silent for any session larger than the window residency**

The count-based `TrajectoryTailer` (`lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart:120-128`) dedupes by list length:

```dart
List<String> tail(List<SessionRecord> records) {
  if (records.length <= _seen) return const [];
  final fresh = records.sublist(_seen);
  _seen = records.length;
  ...
}
```

Composed with this PR's two changes, the headless `tail` verb deadlocks itself:

1. Line 40 (`await session.ensureWholeLedgerResident();`) runs for **every** verb, including `tail`. The initial `tailer.tail(records)` therefore sees the WHOLE ledger (N records — the PR's own `session_tree_test` proves 800 records page in), so `_seen = N`.
2. Each poll re-opens a **fresh windowed** session and calls `getBranch()` — which returns only the ~200-record resident tail window (the rework summary itself notes "200 resident at open").
3. `fresh.length` (~200) `<= _seen` (N) → `tail()` returns `const []` on **every poll, forever**. No error, no exit code change — the command just stops emitting.

This breaks `fa trajectory tail` not only for the incident-class giant sessions but for **any session with more than ~200 records**, which is exactly the population this PR targets. CI stays green because no test exercises the headless tail against a >window session (the `/trajectory tail` test in `trajectory_cli_test.dart` rides the live-session path in `trajectory_commands.dart`, which is a different code path and unaffected).

**Fix options** (either works):

- Poll the *original* `session` object instead of re-opening: after `ensureWholeLedgerResident()` its window covers the whole ledger, and its live-tail ingest (`_ingestAtTail`, `windowed_session_storage.dart:736`) picks up the appended suffix on each `getBranch()`, so the branch list genuinely grows past `_seen`.
- Or skip `ensureWholeLedgerResident()` for the `tail` verb entirely (the tailer never needs the head) — cheaper startup, though the initial print then covers only the resident window instead of the old full-branch parity; if that parity matters, pair it with option 1.

A regression test should seed >window records (e.g. 300), tail headlessly, append, and assert the new record renders — see `comment4` below.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `loadAllOlder` reproduces the heap exhaustion the gh-1073 backstop was built to prevent — with no size guard**

The 2 GiB full-open refusal exists because materializing a giant ledger exhausts the heap. `loadAllOlder()` reaches the same exhaustion through the windowed door: every record above the window is parsed and retained in `_entries` **plus** three indexes (`_byId`, `_offsetById`, `_labelsById`) — for a 2.6 GiB incident-shape ledger that is very likely OOM, reached only after a multi-minute whole-file scan, where the old code failed fast with a clear `SessionErrorCode.tooLarge` message pointing at `fa session repair`.

`ensureWholeLedgerResident()` (called unconditionally from `bin/fah_trajectory.dart:40` for `view`/`cost`/`inspect`) therefore degrades "clean refusal with remediation guidance" into "long hang, then probable VM crash" for exactly the sessions this ticket is about. These surfaces genuinely need the whole ledger today, so this is not a blocker — but until AC3a streaming lands, please add a cheap pre-check (`await _reader.stat()` size vs. a bound, e.g. the same 2 GiB) that throws the same `tooLarge` `SessionException` with the repair hint before the scan starts. That keeps the honest degradation contract (F3 NEG) for the truly-giant case while the chunked scan fixes the merely-large one.

Two smaller notes on the same method:

- If the scan loop breaks early on `chunk.isEmpty` (file truncated below `top` mid-scan), `_hasOlder` is still set to `false` and the window claims full residency over a range that was never read. It follows the `_readOlderBlock` "empty read ends the walk" convention, so consistent — but worth a comment that an early empty read here means *truncation*, not *clean EOF at the head*.
- `_spliceOlderAbove` is byte-for-byte the same splice logic as the new `prepend` block in `_indexChunk` (three `insertAll` + the identical per-record index/`_appendedBelow.remove`/label-cache loop). Extract one shared `_blockPrepend(records, starts, ends)` so the next window-layout change can't update one copy and miss the other.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):

💡 **SUGGESTION: `_spliceOlderAbove` duplicates the block-prepend splice now living in `_indexChunk`**

The body here (three `insertAll(0, …)` calls plus the per-record `_byId` / `_offsetById` / `_appendedBelow.remove` / `updateSessionLabelCache` loop) is identical to the new `prepend` branch of `_indexChunk` at `windowed_session_storage.dart:937-958`. Both were introduced in this PR. Extract a single private `_blockPrepend(List<SessionRecord> records, List<int> starts, List<int> ends)` and call it from both sites — the window-list invariant (three parallel lists kept in the same file order) is exactly the kind of thing that drifts when two copies exist.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):

💡 **SUGGESTION: add a headless `tail` regression test with more records than the residency window**

This test group proves windowed resolution and whole-ledger materialization, but nothing exercises the `tail` verb's poll loop against a session bigger than the ~200-record window residency — which is why the poll-window/`TrajectoryTailer._seen` interaction in `bin/fah_trajectory.dart` (see the BLOCKING finding) ships green. A cheap version: seed ~300 records, run the headless tail verb in a zone/fake clock or factor the poll loop, append one record, and assert a new row renders. Even a pure composition test (`TrajectoryTailer` fed by a fresh windowed open's `getBranch()` after a whole-ledger prime) would have caught the silent-stall.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):

Fixed in `bin/fah_trajectory.dart` + `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart`.

The headless `tail` poll no longer re-opens a fresh windowed session. It now polls the **original** `session` object: after `ensureWholeLedgerResident()` its window covers the whole ledger, and each poll runs the windowed live-tail ingest (`WindowedSessionStorage.ingestAppended()`) before `getBranch()`, so the branch genuinely picks up the appended suffix. The poll loop was extracted into `_runTrajectoryTail` to keep the command dispatcher under the CRAP ratchet.

One layer deeper than the suggested fix: the tailer's dedupe is now **by record id instead of list length**. Polling the original windowed session means the resident window can *slide* (head eviction drops the oldest records as new ones append) once the ledger exceeds the residency cap — the branch list shrinks or holds flat in length while genuinely growing at the tail, so a count-based `_seen` would still have gone silent for exactly the giant-session population this PR targets. `TrajectoryTailer` now keeps a `_seenIds` set; the REPL `/trajectory tail` path sharing the class is strictly more robust too (it was previously only safe because its full-open session never evicted).

Regression coverage (both would have failed on the shipped code):

- `test/cli/trajectory_cli_test.dart` — `TrajectoryTailer` fed a slid window (300-record prime, head-evicted poll) still renders the appended row.
- `test/cli/oversize_session_open_test.dart` — two end-to-end compositions over a 300-record session (> the ~200-record window): the fixed poll (original session + `ingestAppended`) renders the external append, and the exact regression shape (fresh windowed re-open per poll after a whole-ledger prime) also renders it.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):

Fixed in `lib/src/session/windowed_session_storage.dart` (`loadAllOlder`).

Added the cheap pre-check before the scan: `await _reader.stat()` size vs. `maxWholeLedgerBytes` (defaults to `defaultMaxFullOpenBytes`, the same 2 GiB gh-1073 bound), throwing the same `SessionException` with `SessionErrorCode.tooLarge` and the `fa session repair` / gh-1073 remediation wording (sizes formatted by `formatSessionBytes`, the helper behind the full-open message — promoted from private so both refusal sites share it). A truly-giant ledger now fails fast and honestly instead of hanging for minutes and then OOMing; the merely-large one still pages in chunked. The bound is an optional named parameter so the refusal is unit-testable without a 2 GiB fixture.

Both smaller notes addressed:

- The early-empty-read break in `_scanFileHeadStrips` now carries an explicit comment: an empty read below `top` mid-scan means **truncation**, not a clean EOF at the head (the `_readOlderBlock` "empty read ends the walk" convention), and `loadAllOlder`'s `_hasOlder = false` is documented with the same caveat.
- The duplicated splice was extracted as `_blockPrepend(records, starts, ends)` — see thread 3.

New regression test: `test/session/windowed_session_storage_test.dart` — `loadAllOlder` refuses with `tooLarge` + repair hint before paging anything when the file exceeds the bound, and still pages the whole head in when under it.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):

Fixed in `lib/src/session/windowed_session_storage.dart`.

Extracted the single private `_blockPrepend(List<SessionRecord> records, List<int> starts, List<int> ends)` — three parallel `insertAll(0, …)` calls (one memmove per list) plus the per-record re-index (`_byId` / `_offsetById` / `_appendedBelow.remove` / `updateSessionLabelCache`), with a doc noting the window-list invariant it guards and its two callers. `_indexChunk`'s `prepend` branch now builds the three parallel lists and delegates; `_spliceOlderAbove` was removed and `loadAllOlder` calls `_blockPrepend` directly (a one-line delegate would have been needless indirection). The O(n²)→block-prepend history is preserved in `_blockPrepend`'s doc.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-11):

Added in `test/cli/oversize_session_open_test.dart` (new group `headless tail over a >window session`), plus a unit-level case in `test/cli/trajectory_cli_test.dart`.

Two compositions, both seeded with 300 records (> the ~200-record residency window) against the incident-shape `RefusingFullOpenRepo` setup:

1. **The fixed poll path** — windowed resolve → `ensureWholeLedgerResident()` → initial backfill via `TrajectoryTailer` → external append → `ingestAppended()` on the original session's storage → `getBranch()` → asserts the new row (`fresh!`) renders.

This test fails against the old count-based dedupe — it reproduces the silent stall.

A `TrajectoryTailer` unit test (300-record prime, then a head-evicted slid window) covers the eviction-slide case directly.

# gh-1555: [GOAL] Session JSONL grows unboundedly past the 2 GiB full-open backstop; legacy full-open call sites (picker, resume fallback, trajectory, subagent preview) make the session unopenable

## Description

## Goal — unbounded session JSONL growth defeats the 2 GiB full-open backstop (v1, initial draft)

One sentence: **every session remains openable forever at ANY size — 100 GB included — through lazy, tail-first, bounded-memory reads, and no ledger record is ever lost**: size is a read-pattern problem, never a deletion problem.

Today a session JSONL is append-only forever: compaction appends a summary record and never shrinks the file, and nothing rotates or trims by size. The gh-1073 backstop (`defaultMaxFullOpenBytes = 2 << 30`, lib/src/session/session_storage.dart:30) converted the old silent heap explosion into a loud `SessionException` refusal — but nothing on the write side slows growth and nothing on the read side migrates the legacy full-open call sites to the existing windowed reader. So every active named session is a ticking bomb: it works for weeks, then permanently falls off the picker/trajectory/resume-fallback paths. This happened in production on 2026-10-11 (incident below). This card changes both sides: all tail/preview/trajectory read paths migrate to windowed/token-budgeted opens, and the ledger gains a size-based rotation/trim plus write-side caps on the dominant growth drivers.

## Owner directive (2026-10-11, supersedes any size-budget thinking below)

- **Sessions are never lost.** Not by trim, not by rotation, not by repair, not by write-side cap applied retroactively. A 100 GB ledger is a valid ledger. Any solution whose size story involves deleting or truncating EXISTING records is rejected by definition.
- **Openability is unconditional.** Picker, resume, trajectory view, trajectory export, subagent preview — all must work on a 100 GB session with bounded memory. If a path cannot be made lazy, the path is buggy, not the session "too big".
- **Context-meter continuity across close/reopen.** A session closed showing 59% context usage reopens showing the same 59% — the resume boundary (newest compaction boundary, or the token-budget tail for a boundary-less marathon) must reconstruct EXACTLY the context the live loop carried at exit, not an approximation. Wrong boundary = wrong meter = a regression the owner can see.
- **Lazy loading everywhere, export included.** Today `exportTrajectoryJson`/`exportTrajectoryMarkdown` (lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_export.dart:16,33) take a fully materialized `TrajectorySnapshot` — pure functions over `snapshot.records`, no IO. That means export transitively requires the full open it should avoid. Export must become scan-and-emit streaming: read records in bounded chunks, serialize incrementally to the sink, never materialize the snapshot.
- **Forward-looking write-side reduction** (W3) is permitted ONLY as opt-in and only for FUTURE records, and even then is an owner-call open question — never the mechanism that makes old sessions openable.

## Why this framing

- **Retracted framing 1:** "just raise/disable the 2 GiB bound" — the bound exists because a 12 GiB session used to die with `Exhausted heap space` inside readTextFile (gh-1073); raising it re-opens the OOM. Retracted.
- **Retracted framing 2:** "compaction alone fixes size" — compaction APPENDS a summary record; it never shrinks the file. The "network" incident session reached 2.54 GiB with **zero** compaction records; the ssh/followup session reached 2.91 GB **with** 51 compaction records. Compaction reduces model context, not bytes on disk. Retracted.
- **Retracted framing 3:** "this is a read-side-only fix" — migrating call sites keeps the bomb ticking at 0.4–0.6 GB/week; the write side needs caps and a trim story. Retracted as insufficient (kept as the core tier, not the whole card).
- **Retracted framing 4:** "trim/rotate/delete old records to stay under a size budget" — owner directive 2026-10-11: the ledger is sacred, a 100 GB session must open, and no existing record may be lost. Rotation is allowed ONLY as split-and-retain (all `.part-NN` siblings kept and reassembled by the reader); repair keeps its `.bak` until the user explicitly removes it. Retracted.

## Incident (2026-10-11, all numbers measured with `stat -f %z` and `LC_ALL=C grep -c '"type":"compaction"'`)

The owner tried to open two sessions from the fa TUI session picker; both failed with `failed to open session <id>: SessionException: Refusing to open session <path>: … exceeds the 2.0 GiB full-open bound`:

| Session | Created | Bytes | Size | Compaction records |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `01a0d73f` ("network") | 2026-09-25 | 2,737,991,964 | 2.54 GiB | **0** in 2.7 GB of JSONL |
| `e7a689` (.worktrees/issue/355/ssh/followup) | 2026-09-14 | 2,912,096,469 | 2.91 GB | 51 |
| `01a06644` ("goal_builder") | 2026-09-03 | 2,236,083,302 | 2.08 GiB | 6 |

Sessions live under `~/Library/Group Containers/group.dev.fa1.shared/fa/sessions/<slug>/`. Measured growth: ~0.4–0.6 GB/week on active named sessions.

## Mechanism chain (pinned facts — each verified against the working tree 2026-10-11)

- **(a) Append-only forever.** Session JSONL grows monotonically; compaction appends a summary record and never shrinks the file; nothing rotates or trims by size.
- **(b) Growth drivers.** Measured on goal_builder's last 500 MB (10,196 records): hidden `model_request_summary` custom records ≈ **0.7 MB EACH** (one per outbound LLM request — they persist a request-detail snapshot for the trajectory Request tab), plus multi-MB toolResult records (full test-run logs). Top records in the chunk: one 1.5 MB toolResult, then an unbroken run of 0.7 MB model_request_summary records.
- **(c) The windowed tail-reader EXISTS and is the intended design.** `WindowedSessionStorage.open` via `SessionRepo.open(metadata, windowed: true)` at lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:343 (doc comment: "the app's chat path, issue #135 … only the header plus the newest chunk are materialized"). The CLI resume `_loadSession` opens windowed (lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart:582) and pages back only to the newest compaction boundary under a token budget (`ensureCompactionBoundaryResident`, gh-968 parity budget).
- **(d) BUT seven legacy call sites still take the DEFAULT full open (windowed:false):**
  1. lib/src/cli/agent_cli_pickers.dart:74 — TUI session picker `_tuiPickSession` does `_repo.open(metadata)`; the catch at :82 prints exactly the observed `failed to open session <id>: SessionException: Refusing to open session …`. **← the user's exact failure path.**
  2. lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart:611 — `_loadSession` full-open FALLBACK when `ensureCompactionBoundaryResident` returns false (a marathon with NO compaction boundary). The "network" session has 0 compaction records → even the main resume path degenerates to full open → guaranteed refusal past 2 GiB.
  3. lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart:196 — `_resumeLastSession` full open.
  4. lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart:492 — name-resolution fallback loop, full-open PER SESSION until name match.
  5. lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart:64,67,71 — `fa trajectory view/tail/cost/inspect` resolve via `repo.open(metadata)` full.
  6. bin/fah_trajectory.dart:94 — headless trajectory full open.
  7. lib/src/cli/agent_commands.dart:314 — `_openChildSession` (subagent transcript preview) full open.
- **(e) The backstop itself.** `defaultMaxFullOpenBytes = 2 << 30` (lib/src/session/session_storage.dart:30); refusal thrown at :641 and :752 with `SessionErrorCode.tooLarge` (gh-1073 — added because a 12 GiB session used to die with `Exhausted heap space` inside readTextFile).

### Amplification

The backstop converted a silent heap explosion into a loud refusal — but nothing on the WRITE side slows growth, and nothing on the READ side migrates the legacy call sites to windowed. So every long-lived named session is a ticking bomb: it works for weeks, then permanently falls off the picker/trajectory/resume-fallback paths. The gh-1073 refusal message even prescribes `fa --session …` and `fa session repair` — both of which themselves degenerate to a refuse…

# gh-1555: [GOAL] Session JSONL grows unboundedly past the 2 GiB full-open backstop; legacy full-open call sites (picker, resume fallback, trajectory, subagent preview) make the session unopenable

## Description

## Goal — unbounded session JSONL growth defeats the 2 GiB full-open backstop (v1, initial draft)

One sentence: **every session remains openable forever at ANY size — 100 GB included — through lazy, tail-first, bounded-memory reads, and no ledger record is ever lost**: size is a read-pattern problem, never a deletion problem.

Today a session JSONL is append-only forever: compaction appends a summary record and never shrinks the file, and nothing rotates or trims by size. The gh-1073 backstop (`defaultMaxFullOpenBytes = 2 << 30`, lib/src/session/session_storage.dart:30) converted the old silent heap explosion into a loud `SessionException` refusal — but nothing on the write side slows growth and nothing on the read side migrates the legacy full-open call sites to the existing windowed reader. So every active named session is a ticking bomb: it works for weeks, then permanently falls off the picker/trajectory/resume-fallback paths. This happened in production on 2026-10-11 (incident below). This card changes both sides: all tail/preview/trajectory read paths migrate to windowed/token-budgeted opens, and the ledger gains a size-based rotation/trim plus write-side caps on the dominant growth drivers.

## Owner directive (2026-10-11, supersedes any size-budget thinking below)

- **Sessions are never lost.** Not by trim, not by rotation, not by repair, not by write-side cap applied retroactively. A 100 GB ledger is a valid ledger. Any solution whose size story involves deleting or truncating EXISTING records is rejected by definition.
- **Openability is unconditional.** Picker, resume, trajectory view, trajectory export, subagent preview — all must work on a 100 GB session with bounded memory. If a path cannot be made lazy, the path is buggy, not the session "too big".
- **Context-meter continuity across close/reopen.** A session closed showing 59% context usage reopens showing the same 59% — the resume boundary (newest compaction boundary, or the token-budget tail for a boundary-less marathon) must reconstruct EXACTLY the context the live loop carried at exit, not an approximation. Wrong boundary = wrong meter = a regression the owner can see.
- **Lazy loading everywhere, export included.** Today `exportTrajectoryJson`/`exportTrajectoryMarkdown` (lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_export.dart:16,33) take a fully materialized `TrajectorySnapshot` — pure functions over `snapshot.records`, no IO. That means export transitively requires the full open it should avoid. Export must become scan-and-emit streaming: read records in bounded chunks, serialize incrementally to the sink, never materialize the snapshot.
- **Forward-looking write-side reduction** (W3) is permitted ONLY as opt-in and only for FUTURE records, and even then is an owner-call open question — never the mechanism that makes old sessions openable.

## Why this framing

- **Retracted framing 1:** "just raise/disable the 2 GiB bound" — the bound exists because a 12 GiB session used to die with `Exhausted heap space` inside readTextFile (gh-1073); raising it re-opens the OOM. Retracted.
- **Retracted framing 2:** "compaction alone fixes size" — compaction APPENDS a summary record; it never shrinks the file. The "network" incident session reached 2.54 GiB with **zero** compaction records; the ssh/followup session reached 2.91 GB **with** 51 compaction records. Compaction reduces model context, not bytes on disk. Retracted.
- **Retracted framing 3:** "this is a read-side-only fix" — migrating call sites keeps the bomb ticking at 0.4–0.6 GB/week; the write side needs caps and a trim story. Retracted as insufficient (kept as the core tier, not the whole card).
- **Retracted framing 4:** "trim/rotate/delete old records to stay under a size budget" — owner directive 2026-10-11: the ledger is sacred, a 100 GB session must open, and no existing record may be lost. Rotation is allowed ONLY as split-and-retain (all `.part-NN` siblings kept and reassembled by the reader); repair keeps its `.bak` until the user explicitly removes it. Retracted.

## Incident (2026-10-11, all numbers measured with `stat -f %z` and `LC_ALL=C grep -c '"type":"compaction"'`)

The owner tried to open two sessions from the fa TUI session picker; both failed with `failed to open session <id>: SessionException: Refusing to open session <path>: … exceeds the 2.0 GiB full-open bound`:

| Session | Created | Bytes | Size | Compaction records |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `01a0d73f` ("network") | 2026-09-25 | 2,737,991,964 | 2.54 GiB | **0** in 2.7 GB of JSONL |
| `e7a689` (.worktrees/issue/355/ssh/followup) | 2026-09-14 | 2,912,096,469 | 2.91 GB | 51 |
| `01a06644` ("goal_builder") | 2026-09-03 | 2,236,083,302 | 2.08 GiB | 6 |

Sessions live under `~/Library/Group Containers/group.dev.fa1.shared/fa/sessions/<slug>/`. Measured growth: ~0.4–0.6 GB/week on active named sessions.

## Mechanism chain (pinned facts — each verified against the working tree 2026-10-11)

- **(a) Append-only forever.** Session JSONL grows monotonically; compaction appends a summary record and never shrinks the file; nothing rotates or trims by size.
- **(b) Growth drivers.** Measured on goal_builder's last 500 MB (10,196 records): hidden `model_request_summary` custom records ≈ **0.7 MB EACH** (one per outbound LLM request — they persist a request-detail snapshot for the trajectory Request tab), plus multi-MB toolResult records (full test-run logs). Top records in the chunk: one 1.5 MB toolResult, then an unbroken run of 0.7 MB model_request_summary records.
- **(c) The windowed tail-reader EXISTS and is the intended design.** `WindowedSessionStorage.open` via `SessionRepo.open(metadata, windowed: true)` at lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:343 (doc comment: "the app's chat path, issue #135 … only the header plus the newest chunk are materialized"). The CLI resume `_loadSession` opens windowed (lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart:582) and pages back only to the newest compaction boundary under a token budget (`ensureCompactionBoundaryResident`, gh-968 parity budget).
- **(d) BUT seven legacy call sites still take the DEFAULT full open (windowed:false):**
  1. lib/src/cli/agent_cli_pickers.dart:74 — TUI session picker `_tuiPickSession` does `_repo.open(metadata)`; the catch at :82 prints exactly the observed `failed to open session <id>: SessionException: Refusing to open session …`. **← the user's exact failure path.**
  2. lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart:611 — `_loadSession` full-open FALLBACK when `ensureCompactionBoundaryResident` returns false (a marathon with NO compaction boundary). The "network" session has 0 compaction records → even the main resume path degenerates to full open → guaranteed refusal past 2 GiB.
  3. lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart:196 — `_resumeLastSession` full open.
  4. lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart:492 — name-resolution fallback loop, full-open PER SESSION until name match.
  5. lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart:64,67,71 — `fa trajectory view/tail/cost/inspect` resolve via `repo.open(metadata)` full.
  6. bin/fah_trajectory.dart:94 — headless trajectory full open.
  7. lib/src/cli/agent_commands.dart:314 — `_openChildSession` (subagent transcript preview) full open.
- **(e) The backstop itself.** `defaultMaxFullOpenBytes = 2 << 30` (lib/src/session/session_storage.dart:30); refusal thrown at :641 and :752 with `SessionErrorCode.tooLarge` (gh-1073 — added because a 12 GiB session used to die with `Exhausted heap space` inside readTextFile).

### Amplification

The backstop converted a silent heap explosion into a loud refusal — but nothing on the WRITE side slows growth, and nothing on the READ side migrates the legacy call sites to windowed. So every long-lived named session is a ticking bomb: it works for weeks, then permanently falls off the picker/trajectory/resume-fallback paths. The gh-1073 refusal message even prescribes `fa --session …` and `fa session repair` — both of which themselves degenerate to a refuse…

# gh-1555: [GOAL] Session JSONL grows unboundedly past the 2 GiB full-open backstop; legacy full-open call sites (picker, resume fallback, trajectory, subagent preview) make the session unopenable

## Description

## Goal — unbounded session JSONL growth defeats the 2 GiB full-open backstop (v1, initial draft)

One sentence: **every session remains openable forever at ANY size — 100 GB included — through lazy, tail-first, bounded-memory reads, and no ledger record is ever lost**: size is a read-pattern problem, never a deletion problem.

Today a session JSONL is append-only forever: compaction appends a summary record and never shrinks the file, and nothing rotates or trims by size. The gh-1073 backstop (`defaultMaxFullOpenBytes = 2 << 30`, lib/src/session/session_storage.dart:30) converted the old silent heap explosion into a loud `SessionException` refusal — but nothing on the write side slows growth and nothing on the read side migrates the legacy full-open call sites to the existing windowed reader. So every active named session is a ticking bomb: it works for weeks, then permanently falls off the picker/trajectory/resume-fallback paths. This happened in production on 2026-10-11 (incident below). This card changes both sides: all tail/preview/trajectory read paths migrate to windowed/token-budgeted opens, and the ledger gains a size-based rotation/trim plus write-side caps on the dominant growth drivers.

## Owner directive (2026-10-11, supersedes any size-budget thinking below)

- **Sessions are never lost.** Not by trim, not by rotation, not by repair, not by write-side cap applied retroactively. A 100 GB ledger is a valid ledger. Any solution whose size story involves deleting or truncating EXISTING records is rejected by definition.
- **Openability is unconditional.** Picker, resume, trajectory view, trajectory export, subagent preview — all must work on a 100 GB session with bounded memory. If a path cannot be made lazy, the path is buggy, not the session "too big".
- **Context-meter continuity across close/reopen.** A session closed showing 59% context usage reopens showing the same 59% — the resume boundary (newest compaction boundary, or the token-budget tail for a boundary-less marathon) must reconstruct EXACTLY the context the live loop carried at exit, not an approximation. Wrong boundary = wrong meter = a regression the owner can see.
- **Lazy loading everywhere, export included.** Today `exportTrajectoryJson`/`exportTrajectoryMarkdown` (lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_export.dart:16,33) take a fully materialized `TrajectorySnapshot` — pure functions over `snapshot.records`, no IO. That means export transitively requires the full open it should avoid. Export must become scan-and-emit streaming: read records in bounded chunks, serialize incrementally to the sink, never materialize the snapshot.
- **Forward-looking write-side reduction** (W3) is permitted ONLY as opt-in and only for FUTURE records, and even then is an owner-call open question — never the mechanism that makes old sessions openable.

## Why this framing

- **Retracted framing 1:** "just raise/disable the 2 GiB bound" — the bound exists because a 12 GiB session used to die with `Exhausted heap space` inside readTextFile (gh-1073); raising it re-opens the OOM. Retracted.
- **Retracted framing 2:** "compaction alone fixes size" — compaction APPENDS a summary record; it never shrinks the file. The "network" incident session reached 2.54 GiB with **zero** compaction records; the ssh/followup session reached 2.91 GB **with** 51 compaction records. Compaction reduces model context, not bytes on disk. Retracted.
- **Retracted framing 3:** "this is a read-side-only fix" — migrating call sites keeps the bomb ticking at 0.4–0.6 GB/week; the write side needs caps and a trim story. Retracted as insufficient (kept as the core tier, not the whole card).
- **Retracted framing 4:** "trim/rotate/delete old records to stay under a size budget" — owner directive 2026-10-11: the ledger is sacred, a 100 GB session must open, and no existing record may be lost. Rotation is allowed ONLY as split-and-retain (all `.part-NN` siblings kept and reassembled by the reader); repair keeps its `.bak` until the user explicitly removes it. Retracted.

## Incident (2026-10-11, all numbers measured with `stat -f %z` and `LC_ALL=C grep -c '"type":"compaction"'`)

The owner tried to open two sessions from the fa TUI session picker; both failed with `failed to open session <id>: SessionException: Refusing to open session <path>: … exceeds the 2.0 GiB full-open bound`:

| Session | Created | Bytes | Size | Compaction records |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `01a0d73f` ("network") | 2026-09-25 | 2,737,991,964 | 2.54 GiB | **0** in 2.7 GB of JSONL |
| `e7a689` (.worktrees/issue/355/ssh/followup) | 2026-09-14 | 2,912,096,469 | 2.91 GB | 51 |
| `01a06644` ("goal_builder") | 2026-09-03 | 2,236,083,302 | 2.08 GiB | 6 |

Sessions live under `~/Library/Group Containers/group.dev.fa1.shared/fa/sessions/<slug>/`. Measured growth: ~0.4–0.6 GB/week on active named sessions.

## Mechanism chain (pinned facts — each verified against the working tree 2026-10-11)

- **(a) Append-only forever.** Session JSONL grows monotonically; compaction appends a summary record and never shrinks the file; nothing rotates or trims by size.
- **(b) Growth drivers.** Measured on goal_builder's last 500 MB (10,196 records): hidden `model_request_summary` custom records ≈ **0.7 MB EACH** (one per outbound LLM request — they persist a request-detail snapshot for the trajectory Request tab), plus multi-MB toolResult records (full test-run logs). Top records in the chunk: one 1.5 MB toolResult, then an unbroken run of 0.7 MB model_request_summary records.
- **(c) The windowed tail-reader EXISTS and is the intended design.** `WindowedSessionStorage.open` via `SessionRepo.open(metadata, windowed: true)` at lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:343 (doc comment: "the app's chat path, issue #135 … only the header plus the newest chunk are materialized"). The CLI resume `_loadSession` opens windowed (lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart:582) and pages back only to the newest compaction boundary under a token budget (`ensureCompactionBoundaryResident`, gh-968 parity budget).
- **(d) BUT seven legacy call sites still take the DEFAULT full open (windowed:false):**
  1. lib/src/cli/agent_cli_pickers.dart:74 — TUI session picker `_tuiPickSession` does `_repo.open(metadata)`; the catch at :82 prints exactly the observed `failed to open session <id>: SessionException: Refusing to open session …`. **← the user's exact failure path.**
  2. lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart:611 — `_loadSession` full-open FALLBACK when `ensureCompactionBoundaryResident` returns false (a marathon with NO compaction boundary). The "network" session has 0 compaction records → even the main resume path degenerates to full open → guaranteed refusal past 2 GiB.
  3. lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart:196 — `_resumeLastSession` full open.
  4. lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart:492 — name-resolution fallback loop, full-open PER SESSION until name match.
  5. lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart:64,67,71 — `fa trajectory view/tail/cost/inspect` resolve via `repo.open(metadata)` full.
  6. bin/fah_trajectory.dart:94 — headless trajectory full open.
  7. lib/src/cli/agent_commands.dart:314 — `_openChildSession` (subagent transcript preview) full open.
- **(e) The backstop itself.** `defaultMaxFullOpenBytes = 2 << 30` (lib/src/session/session_storage.dart:30); refusal thrown at :641 and :752 with `SessionErrorCode.tooLarge` (gh-1073 — added because a 12 GiB session used to die with `Exhausted heap space` inside readTextFile).

### Amplification

The backstop converted a silent heap explosion into a loud refusal — but nothing on the WRITE side slows growth, and nothing on the READ side migrates the legacy call sites to windowed. So every long-lived named session is a ticking bomb: it works for weeks, then permanently falls off the picker/trajectory/resume-fallback paths. The gh-1073 refusal message even prescribes `fa --session …` and `fa session repair` — both of which themselves degenerate to a refuse…

# gh-1555: [GOAL] Session JSONL grows unboundedly past the 2 GiB full-open backstop; legacy full-open call sites (picker, resume fallback, trajectory, subagent preview) make the session unopenable

## Description

## Goal — unbounded session JSONL growth defeats the 2 GiB full-open backstop (v1, initial draft)

One sentence: **every session remains openable forever at ANY size — 100 GB included — through lazy, tail-first, bounded-memory reads, and no ledger record is ever lost**: size is a read-pattern problem, never a deletion problem.

Today a session JSONL is append-only forever: compaction appends a summary record and never shrinks the file, and nothing rotates or trims by size. The gh-1073 backstop (`defaultMaxFullOpenBytes = 2 << 30`, lib/src/session/session_storage.dart:30) converted the old silent heap explosion into a loud `SessionException` refusal — but nothing on the write side slows growth and nothing on the read side migrates the legacy full-open call sites to the existing windowed reader. So every active named session is a ticking bomb: it works for weeks, then permanently falls off the picker/trajectory/resume-fallback paths. This happened in production on 2026-10-11 (incident below). This card changes both sides: all tail/preview/trajectory read paths migrate to windowed/token-budgeted opens, and the ledger gains a size-based rotation/trim plus write-side caps on the dominant growth drivers.

## Owner directive (2026-10-11, supersedes any size-budget thinking below)

- **Sessions are never lost.** Not by trim, not by rotation, not by repair, not by write-side cap applied retroactively. A 100 GB ledger is a valid ledger. Any solution whose size story involves deleting or truncating EXISTING records is rejected by definition.
- **Openability is unconditional.** Picker, resume, trajectory view, trajectory export, subagent preview — all must work on a 100 GB session with bounded memory. If a path cannot be made lazy, the path is buggy, not the session "too big".
- **Context-meter continuity across close/reopen.** A session closed showing 59% context usage reopens showing the same 59% — the resume boundary (newest compaction boundary, or the token-budget tail for a boundary-less marathon) must reconstruct EXACTLY the context the live loop carried at exit, not an approximation. Wrong boundary = wrong meter = a regression the owner can see.
- **Lazy loading everywhere, export included.** Today `exportTrajectoryJson`/`exportTrajectoryMarkdown` (lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_export.dart:16,33) take a fully materialized `TrajectorySnapshot` — pure functions over `snapshot.records`, no IO. That means export transitively requires the full open it should avoid. Export must become scan-and-emit streaming: read records in bounded chunks, serialize incrementally to the sink, never materialize the snapshot.
- **Forward-looking write-side reduction** (W3) is permitted ONLY as opt-in and only for FUTURE records, and even then is an owner-call open question — never the mechanism that makes old sessions openable.

## Why this framing

- **Retracted framing 1:** "just raise/disable the 2 GiB bound" — the bound exists because a 12 GiB session used to die with `Exhausted heap space` inside readTextFile (gh-1073); raising it re-opens the OOM. Retracted.
- **Retracted framing 2:** "compaction alone fixes size" — compaction APPENDS a summary record; it never shrinks the file. The "network" incident session reached 2.54 GiB with **zero** compaction records; the ssh/followup session reached 2.91 GB **with** 51 compaction records. Compaction reduces model context, not bytes on disk. Retracted.
- **Retracted framing 3:** "this is a read-side-only fix" — migrating call sites keeps the bomb ticking at 0.4–0.6 GB/week; the write side needs caps and a trim story. Retracted as insufficient (kept as the core tier, not the whole card).
- **Retracted framing 4:** "trim/rotate/delete old records to stay under a size budget" — owner directive 2026-10-11: the ledger is sacred, a 100 GB session must open, and no existing record may be lost. Rotation is allowed ONLY as split-and-retain (all `.part-NN` siblings kept and reassembled by the reader); repair keeps its `.bak` until the user explicitly removes it. Retracted.

## Incident (2026-10-11, all numbers measured with `stat -f %z` and `LC_ALL=C grep -c '"type":"compaction"'`)

The owner tried to open two sessions from the fa TUI session picker; both failed with `failed to open session <id>: SessionException: Refusing to open session <path>: … exceeds the 2.0 GiB full-open bound`:

| Session | Created | Bytes | Size | Compaction records |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `01a0d73f` ("network") | 2026-09-25 | 2,737,991,964 | 2.54 GiB | **0** in 2.7 GB of JSONL |
