# gh-1555: [GOAL] Session JSONL grows unboundedly past the 2 GiB full-open backstop; legacy full-open call sites (picker, resume fallback, trajectory, subagent preview) make the session unopenable

## Description

## Goal — unbounded session JSONL growth defeats the 2 GiB full-open backstop (v1, initial draft)

One sentence: **every session remains openable forever at ANY size — 100 GB included — through lazy, tail-first, bounded-memory reads, and no ledger record is ever lost**: size is a read-pattern problem, never a deletion problem.

Today a session JSONL is append-only forever: compaction appends a summary record and never shrinks the file, and nothing rotates or trims by size. The gh-1073 backstop (`defaultMaxFullOpenBytes = 2 << 30`, lib/src/session/session_storage.dart:30) converted the old silent heap explosion into a loud `SessionException` refusal — but nothing on the write side slows growth and nothing on the read side migrates the legacy full-open call sites to the existing windowed reader. So every active named session is a ticking bomb: it works for weeks, then permanently falls off the picker/trajectory/resume-fallback paths. This happened in production on 2026-10-11 (incident below). This card changes both sides: all tail/preview/trajectory read paths migrate to windowed/token-budgeted opens, and the ledger gains a size-based rotation/trim plus write-side caps on the dominant growth drivers.

## Owner directive (2026-10-11, supersedes any size-budget thinking below)

- **Sessions are never lost.** Not by trim, not by rotation, not by repair, not by write-side cap applied retroactively. A 100 GB ledger is a valid ledger. Any solution whose size story involves deleting or truncating EXISTING records is rejected by definition.
- **Openability is unconditional.** Picker, resume, trajectory view, trajectory export, subagent preview — all must work on a 100 GB session with bounded memory. If a path cannot be made lazy, the path is buggy, not the session "too big".
- **Context-meter continuity across close/reopen.** A session closed showing 59% context usage reopens showing the same 59% — the resume boundary (newest compaction boundary, or the token-budget tail for a boundary-less marathon) must reconstruct EXACTLY the context the live loop carried at exit, not an approximation. Wrong boundary = wrong meter = a regression the owner can see.
- **Lazy loading everywhere, export included.** Today `exportTrajectoryJson`/`exportTrajectoryMarkdown` (lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_export.dart:16,33) take a fully materialized `TrajectorySnapshot` — pure functions over `snapshot.records`, no IO. That means export transitively requires the full open it should avoid. Export must become scan-and-emit streaming: read records in bounded chunks, serialize incrementally to the sink, never materialize the snapshot.
- **Forward-looking write-side reduction** (W3) is permitted ONLY as opt-in and only for FUTURE records, and even then is an owner-call open question — never the mechanism that makes old sessions openable.

## Why this framing

- **Retracted framing 1:** "just raise/disable the 2 GiB bound" — the bound exists because a 12 GiB session used to die with `Exhausted heap space` inside readTextFile (gh-1073); raising it re-opens the OOM. Retracted.
- **Retracted framing 2:** "compaction alone fixes size" — compaction APPENDS a summary record; it never shrinks the file. The "network" incident session reached 2.54 GiB with **zero** compaction records; the ssh/followup session reached 2.91 GB **with** 51 compaction records. Compaction reduces model context, not bytes on disk. Retracted.
- **Retracted framing 3:** "this is a read-side-only fix" — migrating call sites keeps the bomb ticking at 0.4–0.6 GB/week; the write side needs caps and a trim story. Retracted as insufficient (kept as the core tier, not the whole card).
- **Retracted framing 4:** "trim/rotate/delete old records to stay under a size budget" — owner directive 2026-10-11: the ledger is sacred, a 100 GB session must open, and no existing record may be lost. Rotation is allowed ONLY as split-and-retain (all `.part-NN` siblings kept and reassembled by the reader); repair keeps its `.bak` until the user explicitly removes it. Retracted.

## Incident (2026-10-11, all numbers measured with `stat -f %z` and `LC_ALL=C grep -c '"type":"compaction"'`)

The owner tried to open two sessions from the fa TUI session picker; both failed with `failed to open session <id>: SessionException: Refusing to open session <path>: … exceeds the 2.0 GiB full-open bound`:

| Session | Created | Bytes | Size | Compaction records |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `01a0d73f` ("network") | 2026-09-25 | 2,737,991,964 | 2.54 GiB | **0** in 2.7 GB of JSONL |
| `e7a689` (.worktrees/issue/355/ssh/followup) | 2026-09-14 | 2,912,096,469 | 2.91 GB | 51 |
| `01a06644` ("goal_builder") | 2026-09-03 | 2,236,083,302 | 2.08 GiB | 6 |

Sessions live under `~/Library/Group Containers/group.dev.fa1.shared/fa/sessions/<slug>/`. Measured growth: ~0.4–0.6 GB/week on active named sessions.

## Mechanism chain (pinned facts — each verified against the working tree 2026-10-11)

- **(a) Append-only forever.** Session JSONL grows monotonically; compaction appends a summary record and never shrinks the file; nothing rotates or trims by size.
- **(b) Growth drivers.** Measured on goal_builder's last 500 MB (10,196 records): hidden `model_request_summary` custom records ≈ **0.7 MB EACH** (one per outbound LLM request — they persist a request-detail snapshot for the trajectory Request tab), plus multi-MB toolResult records (full test-run logs). Top records in the chunk: one 1.5 MB toolResult, then an unbroken run of 0.7 MB model_request_summary records.
- **(c) The windowed tail-reader EXISTS and is the intended design.** `WindowedSessionStorage.open` via `SessionRepo.open(metadata, windowed: true)` at lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:343 (doc comment: "the app's chat path, issue #135 … only the header plus the newest chunk are materialized"). The CLI resume `_loadSession` opens windowed (lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart:582) and pages back only to the newest compaction boundary under a token budget (`ensureCompactionBoundaryResident`, gh-968 parity budget).
- **(d) BUT seven legacy call sites still take the DEFAULT full open (windowed:false):**
  1. lib/src/cli/agent_cli_pickers.dart:74 — TUI session picker `_tuiPickSession` does `_repo.open(metadata)`; the catch at :82 prints exactly the observed `failed to open session <id>: SessionException: Refusing to open session …`. **← the user's exact failure path.**
  2. lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart:611 — `_loadSession` full-open FALLBACK when `ensureCompactionBoundaryResident` returns false (a marathon with NO compaction boundary). The "network" session has 0 compaction records → even the main resume path degenerates to full open → guaranteed refusal past 2 GiB.
  3. lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart:196 — `_resumeLastSession` full open.
  4. lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart:492 — name-resolution fallback loop, full-open PER SESSION until name match.
  5. lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart:64,67,71 — `fa trajectory view/tail/cost/inspect` resolve via `repo.open(metadata)` full.
  6. bin/fah_trajectory.dart:94 — headless trajectory full open.
  7. lib/src/cli/agent_commands.dart:314 — `_openChildSession` (subagent transcript preview) full open.
- **(e) The backstop itself.** `defaultMaxFullOpenBytes = 2 << 30` (lib/src/session/session_storage.dart:30); refusal thrown at :641 and :752 with `SessionErrorCode.tooLarge` (gh-1073 — added because a 12 GiB session used to die with `Exhausted heap space` inside readTextFile).

### Amplification

The backstop converted a silent heap explosion into a loud refusal — but nothing on the WRITE side slows growth, and nothing on the READ side migrates the legacy call sites to windowed. So every long-lived named session is a ticking bomb: it works for weeks, then permanently falls off the picker/trajectory/resume-fallback paths. The gh-1073 refusal message even prescribes `fa --session …` and `fa session repair` — both of which themselves degenerate to a refuse…

## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: The windowed-everywhere migration is well-executed (block-prepend `_indexChunk`, sequential `loadAllOlder`, foreign-repo degradation, incident-shape fixtures), but one BLOCKING regression: the headless `fa trajectory tail` poll re-opens windowed while the tailer dedupes by count after a whole-ledger prime — so tail goes permanently silent for any session larger than the ~200-record residency window (the exact class this PR targets). One IMPORTANT: `loadAllOlder` materializes the whole ledger with no size guard, trading the gh-1073 clean refusal for a long-then-OOM failure mode. **Key Issues**:
1. 🚨 `bin/fah_trajectory.dart:103` — tail poll returns `const []` forever once `_seen` (whole-ledger count) exceeds the windowed branch length
2. ⚠️ `windowed_session_storage.dart:429` — `loadAllOlder` has no pre-scan size bound; giant ledgers OOM instead of failing fast with `tooLarge` + repair hint
3. 💡 `windowed_session_storage.dart:497` — `_spliceOlderAbove` duplicates the `_indexChunk` prepend splice
4. 💡 Test gap: no headless tail test over a >window session

**Next Steps**:
1. Poll the original `session` object (live-tail ingest) or skip the whole-ledger prime for `tail`
2. Add a `stat()`-based size pre-check in `loadAllOlder` throwing the existing `tooLarge` `SessionException` until AC3a streaming lands

## Verification of each review finding (code inspected at head 7cd3e5a3f)

1. 🚨 **BLOCKING — headless `fa trajectory tail` went silent for >window sessions** — FIXED.
   - `bin/fah_trajectory.dart`: the poll loop was extracted into `_runTrajectoryTail` (dispatcher stays under the CRAP ratchet) and now polls the **original** `session` object, running the windowed live-tail ingest (`WindowedSessionStorage.ingestAppended()`) before each `getBranch()` — the branch genuinely picks up the appended suffix.

2. ⚠️ **IMPORTANT — `loadAllOlder` heap exhaustion without a size guard** — FIXED.

The bound is a named parameter, so the refusal is unit-testable without a 2 GiB fixture.

3. 💡 **_blockPrepend extraction** — verified above: exactly one copy of the three-`insertAll` splice + per-record re-index, doc-commented with the window-list invariant and its two callers.
4. 💡 **Headless-tail regression test over a >window session** — present: new group in `test/cli/oversize_session_open_test.dart` seeds 300 records (> the ~200-record window), covers **both** the fixed poll composition (original session + `ingestAppended`, asserts `fresh!` renders) and the exact regression shape (fresh windowed re-open per poll after a whole-ledger prime, asserts `late!` renders — fails against the old count-based dedupe). Important observation: `readForward` does NOT drop the header line. `_scanFileHeadStrips` starts at offset 0 and calls `readForward(0, maxBytes: ...)`. The first entry will be the header line at offset 0 parsed as a record. `parseSessionEntryLine` — does it parse the header line successfully as some record? 1. Does parsing the header line produce a valid SessionRecord or throw? If `parseSessionEntryLine` throws on header lines, `_parseAllLines` skips torn lines — the header line would be dropped as "torn" — fine either way since offset 0 skipped.

Wait — but there's a subtlety: `_parseAllLines` returns entries only for parsed lines; the header parse might succeed (headers and records might share format?). If header line parses as a record with offset 0, it's skipped. If it fails to parse, it's excluded from entries, and then `ends` computation for the record preceding... actually the header is first, entries[1] would be the first real record with offset > 0. `ends` uses next entry's offset — consistent since entries are contiguous lines parsed. Fine.

2. Bigger issue: `_scanFileHeadStrips` reads `[0, top)` with `readForward`, which sets `limitOffset = lastKeptEnd` (end of last kept record). The loop: `final next = chunk.limitOffset; if (next <= offset) break; offset = next;`. Since readForward is capped by maxBytes budget = min(top - offset, maxWalkBlockBytes 64MB). limitOffset = end of last kept record. Progress guaranteed unless chunk empty (break) — fine.

3. Concurrency: `loadAllOlder` scans file head while a concurrent append writes at tail — appends are below `top`, no overlap. Records at/above top skipped. OK.

4. Concurrent appends BELOW top but above window? Can't happen — window is anchored at tail; region [top, fileSize) is the window's own + appends. Skip via `entry.offset >= top`. But what about `_appendedBelow` records that were appended while deep-paged... in the trajectory headless context no deep paging. Fine.

5. `_windowTopOffset = scanned.starts.first` — only if not empty; if empty (all skipped — e.g. header only), `_windowTopOffset` stays `top` and `_hasOlder = false`. Hmm — is that correct? If scan found nothing (say all lines between 0 and top were torn/skipped), claiming full residency with window top at `top` — records in [0, top) that failed to parse are dropped; claiming residency anyway. Edge case; acceptable, matches truncation convention.

For the tail path over a >2GiB ledger this throws tooLarge → `fa trajectory tail` fails on the incident sessions. AC3 requires tail to work on >2GiB. The old code also failed (full open refused). The prior review's focus was the >window/<=2GiB silence bug. The >2GiB tail failure was pre-existing (full-open refused too). Hmm, but per ticket AC3 this PR is supposed to make tail work on >2GiB. Under W1, tail could trivially work windowed (skip the prime). The rework chose whole-ledger backfill parity instead. The tooLarge pre-check now actively prevents tail on >2GiB sessions — a session class the ticket is explicitly about. I'd rate this IMPORTANT: skip `ensureWholeLedgerResident` for the `tail` verb (tailer needs only the tail; the initial print covering only the resident window is a parity trade-off worth a comment), or catch. This is an AC3 gap, not a regression. IMPORTANT seems right.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: `_seenIds` grows unboundedly over a long-running tail**

The id-based dedupe is the right fix for the slid-window silent-stall (and strictly more robust than the old count). A cheap bound: when the set exceeds the residency cap by some factor, drop the ids of records that are no longer reachable from the current branch (or simply cap to the newest N ids and accept a theoretical duplicate render after a truncation re-anchor). # gh-1555: [GOAL] Session JSONL grows unboundedly past the 2 GiB full-open backstop; legacy full-open call sites (picker, resume fallback, trajectory, subagent preview) make the session unopenable

## Description

## Goal — unbounded session JSONL growth defeats the 2 GiB full-open backstop (v1, initial draft)

One sentence: **every session remains openable forever at ANY size — 100 GB included — through lazy, tail-first, bounded-memory reads, and no ledger record is ever lost**: size is a read-pattern problem, never a deletion problem.

Today a session JSONL is append-only forever: compaction appends a summary record and never shrinks the file, and nothing rotates or trims by size. The gh-1073 backstop (`defaultMaxFullOpenBytes = 2 << 30`, lib/src/session/session_storage.dart:30) converted the old silent heap explosion into a loud `SessionException` refusal — but nothing on the write side slows growth and nothing on the read side migrates the legacy full-open call sites to the existing windowed reader. So every active named session is a ticking bomb: it works for weeks, then permanently falls off the picker/trajectory/resume-fallback paths. This happened in production on 2026-10-11 (incident below). This card changes both sides: all tail/preview/trajectory read paths migrate to windowed/token-budgeted opens, and the ledger gains a size-based rotation/trim plus write-side caps on the dominant growth drivers.

## Owner directive (2026-10-11, supersedes any size-budget thinking below)

- **Sessions are never lost.** Not by trim, not by rotation, not by repair, not by write-side cap applied retroactively. A 100 GB ledger is a valid ledger. Any solution whose size story involves deleting or truncating EXISTING records is rejected by definition.
- **Openability is unconditional.** Picker, resume, trajectory view, trajectory export, subagent preview — all must work on a 100 GB session with bounded memory. If a path cannot be made lazy, the path is buggy, not the session "too big".
- **Context-meter continuity across close/reopen.** A session closed showing 59% context usage reopens showing the same 59% — the resume boundary (newest compaction boundary, or the token-budget tail for a boundary-less marathon) must reconstruct EXACTLY the context the live loop carried at exit, not an approximation. Wrong boundary = wrong meter = a regression the owner can see.
- **Lazy loading everywhere, export included.** Today `exportTrajectoryJson`/`exportTrajectoryMarkdown` (lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_export.dart:16,33) take a fully materialized `TrajectorySnapshot` — pure functions over `snapshot.records`, no IO. That means export transitively requires the full open it should avoid. Export must become scan-and-emit streaming: read records in bounded chunks, serialize incrementally to the sink, never materialize the snapshot.
- **Forward-looking write-side reduction** (W3) is permitted ONLY as opt-in and only for FUTURE records, and even then is an owner-call open question — never the mechanism that makes old sessions openable.

## Why this framing

- **Retracted framing 1:** "just raise/disable the 2 GiB bound" — the bound exists because a 12 GiB session used to die with `Exhausted heap space` inside readTextFile (gh-1073); raising it re-opens the OOM. Retracted.
- **Retracted framing 2:** "compaction alone fixes size" — compaction APPENDS a summary record; it never shrinks the file. The "network" incident session reached 2.54 GiB with **zero** compaction records; the ssh/followup session reached 2.91 GB **with** 51 compaction records. Compaction reduces model context, not bytes on disk. Retracted.
- **Retracted framing 3:** "this is a read-side-only fix" — migrating call sites keeps the bomb ticking at 0.4–0.6 GB/week; the write side needs caps and a trim story. Retracted as insufficient (kept as the core tier, not the whole card).
- **Retracted framing 4:** "trim/rotate/delete old records to stay under a size budget" — owner directive 2026-10-11: the ledger is sacred, a 100 GB session must open, and no existing record may be lost. Rotation is allowed ONLY as split-and-retain (all `.part-NN` siblings kept and reassembled by the reader); repair keeps its `.bak` until the user explicitly removes it. Retracted.

## Incident (2026-10-11, all numbers measured with `stat -f %z` and `LC_ALL=C grep -c '"type":"compaction"'`)

The owner tried to open two sessions from the fa TUI session picker; both failed with `failed to open session <id>: SessionException: Refusing to open session <path>: … exceeds the 2.0 GiB full-open bound`:

| Session | Created | Bytes | Size | Compaction records |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `01a0d73f` ("network") | 2026-09-25 | 2,737,991,964 | 2.54 GiB | **0** in 2.7 GB of JSONL |
| `e7a689` (.worktrees/issue/355/ssh/followup) | 2026-09-14 | 2,912,096,469 | 2.91 GB | 51 |
| `01a06644` ("goal_builder") | 2026-09-03 | 2,236,083,302 | 2.08 GiB | 6 |

Sessions live under `~/Library/Group Containers/group.dev.fa1.shared/fa/sessions/<slug>/`. Measured growth: ~0.4–0.6 GB/week on active named sessions.

## Mechanism chain (pinned facts — each verified against the working tree 2026-10-11)

- **(a) Append-only forever.** Session JSONL grows monotonically; compaction appends a summary record and never shrinks the file; nothing rotates or trims by size.
- **(b) Growth drivers.** Measured on goal_builder's last 500 MB (10,196 records): hidden `model_request_summary` custom records ≈ **0.7 MB EACH** (one per outbound LLM request — they persist a request-detail snapshot for the trajectory Request tab), plus multi-MB toolResult records (full test-run logs). Top records in the chunk: one 1.5 MB toolResult, then an unbroken run of 0.7 MB model_request_summary records.
- **(c) The windowed tail-reader EXISTS and is the intended design.** `WindowedSessionStorage.open` via `SessionRepo.open(metadata, windowed: true)` at lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:343 (doc comment: "the app's chat path, issue #135 … only the header plus the newest chunk are materialized"). The CLI resume `_loadSession` opens windowed (lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart:582) and pages back only to the newest compaction boundary under a token budget (`ensureCompactionBoundaryResident`, gh-968 parity budget).
- **(d) BUT seven legacy call sites still take the DEFAULT full open (windowed:false):**
  1. lib/src/cli/agent_cli_pickers.dart:74 — TUI session picker `_tuiPickSession` does `_repo.open(metadata)`; the catch at :82 prints exactly the observed `failed to open session <id>: SessionException: Refusing to open session …`. **← the user's exact failure path.**
  2. lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart:611 — `_loadSession` full-open FALLBACK when `ensureCompactionBoundaryResident` returns false (a marathon with NO compaction boundary). The "network" session has 0 compaction records → even the main resume path degenerates to full open → guaranteed refusal past 2 GiB.
  3. lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart:196 — `_resumeLastSession` full open.
  4. lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart:492 — name-resolution fallback loop, full-open PER SESSION until name match.
  5. lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart:64,67,71 — `fa trajectory view/tail/cost/inspect` resolve via `repo.open(metadata)` full.
  6. bin/fah_trajectory.dart:94 — headless trajectory full open.
  7. lib/src/cli/agent_commands.dart:314 — `_openChildSession` (subagent transcript preview) full open.
- **(e) The backstop itself.** `defaultMaxFullOpenBytes = 2 << 30` (lib/src/session/session_storage.dart:30); refusal thrown at :641 and :752 with `SessionErrorCode.tooLarge` (gh-1073 — added because a 12 GiB session used to die with `Exhausted heap space` inside readTextFile).

### Amplification

The backstop converted a silent heap explosion into a loud refusal — but nothing on the WRITE side slows growth, and nothing on the READ side migrates the legacy call sites to windowed. So every long-lived named session is a ticking bomb: it works for weeks, then permanently falls off the picker/trajectory/resume-fallback paths. The gh-1073 refusal message even prescribes `fa --session …` and `fa session repair` — both of which themselves degenerate to a refuse…

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: `_seenIds` grows unboundedly over a long-running tail**

The id-based dedupe is the right fix for the slid-window silent-stall (and strictly more robust than the old count). One side effect: `_seenIds` accumulates every record id ever seen for the lifetime of the `TrajectoryTailer`, and both the headless `fa trajectory tail` and the REPL `/trajectory tail` follow until interrupted — a tail held open for days on a busy session accumulates millions of id strings.

Since the window only ever slides forward on an append-only ledger, ids can never legitimately re-enter the render path after falling out of residency. A cheap bound: when the set exceeds the residency cap by some factor, drop the ids of records that are no longer reachable from the current branch (or simply cap to the newest N ids and accept a theoretical duplicate render after a truncation re-anchor). Not blocking — just worth a comment or a bound before a long-lived tail becomes a slow leak.
